title: Fix SefariaRef.titlePart/addressPart to match the documented chapter:verse split (or fix the docs)
rule: Evans (ubiquitous-language contract) / TQ-7-TQ-8 spirit (test encodes the bug instead of catching it)
why: The class docstring's own worked example says titlePart of "Mishnah Berakhot 1:1" is "Mishnah Berakhot" (address "1:1"). The `_splitTail` regex only strips a single trailing digit run (optionally +1 letter), so it can never cross the ':' in a chapter:verse address — for that exact documented example it actually produces titlePart == "Mishnah Berakhot 1:" and addressPart == "1". The test file's own inline comment ('let's assert what we actually produce... The SefariaRef titlePart splits on the LAST pure-numeric token') shows the author noticed the mismatch and wrote the test to lock in the wrong output rather than fix the regex or the docs. Mishnah/Tanach chapter:verse is the single most common ref shape in this Torah-study app, so any future caller of titlePart/addressPart (currently unused in production) inherits silently wrong output for the primary case, with a green regression test giving false confidence.
recommendation: Either extend `_splitTail` to also recognize a `\d+:\d+` chapter:verse tail as one address token, or correct the docstring to describe the actual single-digit-run behavior — then update the test to assert the corrected contract, not the current output.
acceptance_criteria: SefariaRef.parse('Mishnah Berakhot 1:1').titlePart equals whatever the corrected docstring promises (either 'Mishnah Berakhot' with the regex fixed, or the docstring rewritten to match current behavior).
sefaria_ref_test.dart's titlePart test for chapter:verse refs no longer contains a comment acknowledging the assertion doesn't match the documented contract.
